resources.string: NCC template matching + Hu-moment shape classification

A 64×64 template is cropped from the image center (yellow box) and searched over the whole image by normalized cross correlation for the best match (red box), with a similarity heatmap output. NCC is invariant to illumination gain/bias changes.

Complete pattern recognition pipeline \"feature extraction → classification\": the shape library (5 classes × 4 transformed copies) pre-extracts log-Hu features; pick a query shape with optional rotation/scale transform, and the nearest-neighbor classifier outputs the class and confidence — verifying the translation/rotation/scale invariance of Hu moments.
Not classified yet. Pick a query shape and transform, then tap \"Extract Features & Classify\".

Image recognition principle (Ch.11):
① Template matching (Eq. 11-1): NCC(x,y)=Σ[(f-μf)(t-μt)]/sqrt(Σ(f-μf)²·Σ(t-μt)²), in [-1,1]. Mean removal in the numerator cancels illumination bias and normalization in the denominator cancels gain, so NCC is invariant to linear illumination changes; the search uses a coarse-to-fine pyramid (full search at 1/4 resolution + refinement at full resolution) to cut computation.
② Hu moments: 7 invariants constructed from central moments of a binary image, invariant to translation/rotation/scale; log transform H'=-sign(H)·lg|H| compresses dynamic range in practice.
③ Classification: nearest neighbor (K=1 special case of KNN) decides by Euclidean distance in log-Hu space, confidence=1/(1+d).
④ Video applications: see "Video Image Recognition" — template tracking (temporal template matching) and frame-difference motion detection.

Per-frame recognition of the video: ① template tracking — the first frame\'s center region serves as the template, and each frame searches within a neighborhood of the previous position by NCC (temporal extension of template matching); ② frame-difference motion detection — adjacent frames are differenced and binarized to measure motion. Software decoding; may take seconds to tens of seconds.

Conclusion: the track hit rate reflects how trackable the template (first-frame center region) is across the video; the motion-ratio curve reflects scene activity — together they form a recognition description of the video content.

Video image recognition principle (Ch.11):
① Template tracking: frame t performs NCC search (Eq. 11-1) within a ±32-pixel neighborhood of frame t-1's position (x,y); the maximum position becomes the target's new position — extending template matching from a single image to the time axis, i.e. object tracking. If the target's appearance changes or it is occluded, the score drops below 0.5 and tracking is declared lost.
② Frame-difference motion detection: D(x,y,t)=|f(x,y,t)-f(x,y,t-1)|, binarized (threshold 25) to measure the changed-pixel ratio and bounding box — the cheapest motion detection method (basis of motion analysis).
③ The two recognitions are complementary: tracking answers "where the target is" and motion detection answers "where motion is" — the foundation of video content analysis and intelligent surveillance.
